text.p: These are the leading stories in Botswana's press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Botswana's infant mortality rate will increase drastically unless hospitals are allowed to prescribe the anit-HIV drug AZT (Azidothymidine), say researchers. There had been a three-fold increase in infant deaths and this was wholly attribitable to AIDS, said Dr Alexander Mushi, head of the paediatric unit of the country's major hospital.
- Seventeen year old Mpule Kwelagobe is Miss Botswana 1997 and will represent her country in the 1997 Miss World Pageant.
- Botswana Ash faces a strike as workers demand an increase in wages and an investigation into allegations of mismanagement.
- A team of doctors led by a professor from the Harvard Research Institute has found that the AIDS virus prevalent in Botswana is more virulent than most others.
- The Botswana Law Society, which was established early this year, has already received 80 complaints of unprofessional conduct by lawyers who are members of the society.
